title: Excessive identification through collection of government ID during registration
description: The registration flow includes a government ID together with email, name, password, and a six-digit code. Collecting a strong real-world identifier at account creation can enable direct identification of the parent beyond what may be necessary for basic authentication, especially if identity proofing is not strictly required at this stage.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication service does not strictly need government ID for initial account creation, or that a less identifying verification method could suffice.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort based on LINDDUN identification/excessive identification logic; exact sub-node label may differ in the canonical threat tree.

title: Linkability of registration data across services or records
description: Combining email, full name, government ID, and registration code in one inbound flow creates a highly unique attribute set. If reused across systems or internal datasets, these attributes can allow records about the same parent to be linked across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the received identifiers may be stored, reused, or correlated with other datasets rather than being immediately minimized or transformed.
uncertainty_note: Sub-node chosen by best judgement for linkability arising from a unique combination of identifiers in a data flow.

title: Disclosure of highly sensitive registration data in transit or at intake
description: This flow carries email, password, name, government ID, and a six-digit code into the authentication service. Interception, logging, debugging capture, or insecure intake handling could disclose credentials and identity data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes there is some risk of inadequate transport protection, endpoint logging, or insufficient protection at the receiving process.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; threat clearly fits information disclosure on the flow/process.

title: Unawareness about purpose and necessity of government ID collection
description: The parent may not understand why a government ID and six-digit code are required during registration, how they will be used, how long they will be retained, or whether they are mandatory. This creates a risk that the data subject cannot make an informed privacy decision when submitting the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the registration interface or notice may not clearly explain purpose, legal basis, retention, and optionality of each field.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is grounded in LINDDUN detectability/unawareness around insufficient transparency to the data subject.

title: Non-compliant collection of special or high-risk identity data
description: Collecting government ID at registration may violate data minimization, necessity, proportionality, or purpose-limitation requirements if not justified for authentication. Handling passwords alongside identity documents also raises compliance obligations for secure processing and storage.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy regulation requires necessity and minimization for identity data collection and secure handling of authentication secrets.
uncertainty_note: Specific compliance basis depends on jurisdiction and business purpose; threat is genuine if government ID is not strictly necessary.

title: Excessive storage of parent account data
description: The flow stores parent account data in the users collection. If more personal data than strictly necessary is persisted, or if highly sensitive parent attributes are stored without need, the datastore becomes a source of avoidable disclosure because retained data may later be accessed, shared, or breached.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account contains personal data such as identifiers, contact details, or credentials/profile attributes, and that the schema may permit storing more fields than are strictly required for authentication/account management.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is based on best judgment for a minimality/avoidable disclosure issue; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->DataStore flows but does not provide the exact subtree id.

title: Stored parent account enables identification of the parent
description: Persisting parent account records in the users collection may directly identify a natural person through names, email addresses, phone numbers, account IDs, or combinations of attributes. If identification is not necessary for all intended purposes, the datastore creates an identification risk.
assumptions: Assumes the stored parent account includes direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id may differ in the full LINDDUN Pro tree; applicability of Identification to stored account data is high-confidence.

title: Parent accounts may be linkable across services or records
description: If the users collection stores stable identifiers, shared email addresses, device/account references, or other persistent attributes, records about a parent may be linked across sessions, children accounts, products, or external datasets. This can reveal broader behavior or relationships than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or correlatable attributes are stored and reused beyond a single isolated account-creation event.
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on schema and reuse of identifiers; included because account storage commonly introduces persistent correlators.

title: Insufficient transparency about storing parent account data
description: When parent account information is stored in the users collection, the parent may not understand what data is retained, for how long, for which purposes, and with whom it may be shared. This undermines users' ability to remain aware of processing affecting their data.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not fully communicate storage purposes, fields, retention, or downstream uses at the point this data is stored.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is plausible for account-storage flows but depends on the surrounding notice/UX, which is not shown in the DFD.

title: Storing parent account data without adequate legal basis or minimization
description: The flow may store parent account personal data in the users collection without a clearly defined lawful basis, purpose limitation, retention limit, or data-minimization controls. This creates risk of non-compliance with privacy/data-protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes governance controls for lawful basis, retention, purpose limitation, and minimization may be incomplete or not enforced at persistence time.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance cannot be confirmed from the DFD alone; this is a governance risk commonly associated with account-data persistence.

title: JWT and user data are identifiable to the parent recipient
description: The authentication response contains a JWT together with user data sent from the Authentication Service to the Parent User. The included claims or user attributes can directly identify, or make identifiable, the authenticated person and link the message to a specific account or household member.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains subject/account claims or the accompanying user data includes personal identifiers or persistent account attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include identifiable-information subtree details.

title: Authentication response discloses personal data beyond what is necessary
description: Sending a JWT plus user data to the Parent User may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the immediate authentication purpose, especially if the token or payload contains profile attributes, child-related data, roles, or other embedded claims visible to the recipient or client environment.
assumptions: Assumes the response includes more than a minimal session artifact and may expose readable claims or user-profile fields.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure scope depends on the concrete JWT claims and user-data fields returned.

title: Authentication message creates attributable evidence of user activity
description: The authentication response and associated token can serve as evidence that a specific user account authenticated at a particular time. This creates attributable records that may later be used to prove or infer the user's actions or presence in the system.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT, logs, or correlated metadata contain account identifiers, timestamps, or session identifiers that can be linked back to the parent user.

title: Parent user may be unaware of personal data shared in the authentication response
description: The Parent User may not be aware of the full extent of personal data contained in the JWT and accompanying user data, such as embedded claims, identifiers, role information, or retention implications. This can prevent informed understanding of what personal data is being shared during sign-in.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain the categories of data included in the token/response or their downstream use.

title: Authentication response may be unnecessary or excessive relative to purpose
description: Providing both a JWT and additional user data to the Parent User may conflict with data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations if only a session token or a smaller attribute set is needed to complete authentication. Excessive account data in the flow can therefore create a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the system's stated purpose for this flow is authentication/session establishment rather than profile delivery.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include non-compliance subtree details.

title: Credential interception exposes highly sensitive child-account login data
description: The flow carries parent email and password from the child user to the authentication service. If the transmission is not adequately protected in transit, an observer or intermediary could learn the parent email address and password, directly exposing personal data and authentication secrets tied to the child account.
assumptions: Assumes the login flow could be observed by network attackers, compromised endpoints, or intermediaries if transport/session protections are weak or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best-fit LINDDUN Pro judgement for information disclosure on a data flow; exact subnode naming may vary by threat-tree edition.

title: Parent email in login flow may enable identification of the child or household
description: Using a parent email address as a login identifier can make the child account indirectly identifiable. Anyone seeing the flow or logs may associate the child session with a specific parent or household, reducing anonymity and increasing the ability to identify the data subject behind the account.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is unique or otherwise attributable to a real person and is visible in transit, application traces, or operational logs.
uncertainty_note: This is a best-fit detectability/identifiability threat on the flow because the identifier is explicit; exact tree-node may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Repeated login submissions can be linked to the same child or family account
description: The stable parent email used during login allows multiple authentication attempts and sessions to be linked together over time. Even without successful authentication, repeated submissions may let the service or observers correlate activity patterns of the same child/family account.
assumptions: Assumes the same parent email is reused across sessions and that the service or other parties can observe or store these submissions.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is assigned by best judgement for linkability caused by stable identifiers in a data flow.

title: Lack of privacy-preserving proof around login attempts may enable over-collection of attributable evidence
description: Authentication events commonly create detailed logs containing parent email, timestamps, device metadata, and outcome status. If the service records excessive attributable evidence for each login attempt, the user may have limited plausible deniability regarding attempted access, creating a non-repudiation privacy threat.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication service logs login attempts with identifying metadata and retains them beyond what is necessary for security and fraud prevention.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on how login auditing is implemented; this threat is about privacy-invasive non-repudiation evidence rather than security logging per se.

title: Child login may collect more personal data than necessary for authentication
description: This flow uses parent email plus password for a child login. If the parent email is not strictly necessary, or if the system reuses it for secondary purposes without proper legal basis, the authentication flow risks collecting personal data that is not compliant with data minimization, purpose limitation, or child-data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdictional requirements apply for children's data and that alternative, less identifying authentication mechanisms may be feasible.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance/privacy-design concern inferred from the data elements in the flow; exact legal applicability depends on system context and jurisdiction.

title: JWT and child profile payload can enable linkability across sessions or services
description: The authentication service sends a JWT identifying the recipient as a child user together with child profile data. If the token contains a stable subject identifier or other persistent claims, and the profile data includes consistent identifiers, the child can be linked across sessions, devices, or relying contexts beyond what is necessary for login.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT or profile payload contains stable identifiers, persistent pseudonyms, or other recurring attributes rather than short-lived, context-specific values.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may vary depending on the JWT claim set and profile schema.

title: Authentication response may disclose excessive child identity information
description: Returning child profiles along with the JWT may reveal more identity-related data than is required for authentication, such as full name, age, avatar, preferences, household relationships, or internal identifiers. This increases the amount of personally identifiable information exposed in a single flow to the child endpoint and any observers with access to that endpoint.
assumptions: Assumes the profile object contains personal or account attributes beyond the minimum needed to establish the authenticated session.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node is approximate because the profile fields are not enumerated in the prompt.

title: JWT claims and profile data may allow inference of sensitive child characteristics
description: Even if the response does not explicitly include special-category data, JWT claims and child profile fields can reveal or support inference about age bracket, parental controls, school status, region, behavior patterns, or account restrictions. For child accounts, such inferences are particularly privacy-relevant.
assumptions: Assumes token claims or profile attributes encode role, age-related flags, restrictions, or other metadata from which sensitive traits can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on the actual semantics of the child profile and JWT claims.

title: The flow may expose a child account's presence and profile details to unauthorized observers
description: If the authentication response is delivered or stored insecurely on the client side, or displayed in a way accessible to other local users, the JWT and child profiles could be disclosed to parties who should not access the child's account information. This creates a confidentiality risk for both authentication credentials and profile data.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate transport protection, insecure client-side storage, logging, browser exposure, or local device sharing could expose the response.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine threat for authentication responses generally, but exact exposure paths are not specified.

title: The child may be unaware that profile data is returned as part of authentication
description: Bundling child profiles with the JWT can reduce transparency if the user is not clearly informed which profile fields are sent at login, for what purpose, and to which client context. For child users, limited understanding of the data exchange can further weaken awareness.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or privacy notices do not clearly explain the authentication response contents and purposes.
uncertainty_note: Applies primarily when the system does not provide age-appropriate transparency around login data.

title: Returning child profiles with authentication may exceed data-minimization and child-privacy obligations
description: Combining authentication with delivery of child profile data may process and disclose more personal data than necessary for the purpose of login. For child accounts, this can conflict with heightened legal obligations around data minimization, purpose limitation, and age-appropriate privacy protections if the extra profile data is not strictly needed at this step.
assumptions: Assumes some profile fields are not necessary for immediate authentication/session establishment and that child-specific regulatory requirements apply.
uncertainty_note: Specific legal non-compliance depends on jurisdiction and the actual profile contents, but the minimization concern is strong.

title: Profile linking through combined child identifiers and attributes
description: The child-profile creation flow combines directly identifying and quasi-identifying attributes—name, date of birth, gender, and government ID—into a single profile record. This enables strong linkage of the child profile across sessions, records, or connected services, and may allow correlation with other datasets beyond what is necessary for profile setup.
assumptions: Child Profile Management stores or otherwise uses these attributes together as one profile and may later correlate them with other records or services.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for a linking-at-data-flow/profile-creation scenario; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may vary by version.

title: Identification of the child from submitted registration data
description: The flow contains explicit identifiers and highly distinguishing attributes, especially government ID together with name and date of birth. These data make the child directly identifiable within the system and potentially to any party with access to the transmitted or processed data.
assumptions: Government ID is unique or near-unique and is retained or processed by Child Profile Management.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; threat applicability itself is strong given the presence of direct identifiers.

title: Exposure of sensitive child personal data during profile creation
description: The profile-creation flow transmits sensitive personal data about a child, including government ID and date of birth. If the flow is insufficiently protected or unnecessarily broad, unauthorized parties could learn private facts about the child, creating a disclosure of information threat.
assumptions: The flow may traverse networks, logs, intermediaries, or application components where access is broader than strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure on an ExternalEntity->Process data flow.

title: Unawareness about extent and purpose of child data collection
description: The parent may not be adequately informed, at the moment of submission, why each field is required—particularly government ID and gender—how long the data will be kept, who will access it, and whether it will be reused for verification, analytics, or sharing. This creates a risk that the data subject and parent are unaware of relevant processing.
assumptions: Just-in-time notices, clear explanations, or layered privacy information may be absent or insufficient in the profile-creation interface.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on interface and notice design not described in the prompt; included because the flow requests substantial child data.

title: Potential collection of child profile attributes beyond necessity or lawful basis
description: Collecting name, date of birth, gender, and especially government ID at profile-creation time may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose unless each attribute is justified. For a child account, such collection raises data minimization, purpose limitation, and child-specific compliance concerns if not clearly required and lawfully grounded.
assumptions: Not all listed attributes are strictly necessary for initial child profile creation, or the lawful basis/parental authorization controls are not fully established.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate. Applicability is strongest if government ID or gender are optional from a functional perspective.

title: Excessive child-profile data stored in childprofiles collection
description: The flow stores or updates child profiles in MongoDB. If the profile schema or update operations include more personal data than is strictly necessary for child-profile management, the datastore will retain avoidable personal data about a child, increasing explicit data disclosure risk through over-collection and over-retention.
assumptions: Child profiles contain personal data about minors and may include optional or sensitive attributes beyond the minimum needed for the service.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimization structure; exact node label may vary by version.

title: Unauthorized modification of child profile during store/update
description: On this write flow, insufficient authorization, validation, or concurrency control could allow a child profile to be altered incorrectly or by an unauthorized actor via the Child Profile Management process, compromising the accuracy and integrity of personal data stored for the child.
assumptions: The process accepts profile updates from upstream actors or services and writes them to the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro integrity subtree numbering may differ; threat applicability is high for a write/update flow.

title: Profile changes may be non-repudiable due to missing audit trail
description: If the process stores or updates child profiles without recording who initiated the change, when it occurred, and what was changed, users or operators may later be unable to prove or dispute actions affecting a child's personal data. This undermines accountability for profile modifications.
assumptions: There is no immutable or reliable audit logging tied to profile write operations.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best judgement; non-repudiation threat is grounded in lack of evidence for profile updates rather than confirmed logging design.

title: Stored child-profile records may be difficult to keep current or corrected
description: Once written to the childprofiles collection, profile data may become outdated, inconsistent, or duplicated if update semantics are weak or corrections are not propagated properly. This can prevent data subjects from ensuring their child-profile data remains accurate and up to date.
assumptions: The application may support multiple updates, partial writes, or denormalized child-profile attributes.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on actual update and correction mechanisms; exact LINDDUN Pro unawareness subtree id may differ.

title: Child profile is stored without enforceable consent or lawful-basis checks
description: If the process writes or updates a child's profile without verifying parental authorization, consent status, age-related policy, or another valid legal basis, the system may process a minor's personal data in a way that is non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Child-profile processing is subject to child-specific consent or lawful-basis requirements.
uncertainty_note: Exact node numbering may vary; compliance risk depends on jurisdiction and the service's chosen legal basis.

title: Search, like, and comment requests can be linked to the same child profile over time
description: The Video Management Service receives repeated search queries, video requests, likes, and comments from the child user. If these events are stored or correlated under a persistent account, device, IP address, or identifier, the service can link actions across sessions and build a detailed behavioral profile of the child.
assumptions: Assumes the service can observe stable identifiers or metadata across requests and retains event logs.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement for linkability of multiple actions on one incoming flow; exact node id may vary by threat-tree edition.

title: Search queries and engagement actions may identify or single out the child
description: Search terms, requested videos, likes, and especially free-text comments may contain or reveal personal information, preferences, routines, or unusual interests. Combined with network and account metadata, the incoming flow may allow the service to identify or single out the child user.
assumptions: Assumes comments or queries can contain personal data and that the service has access to associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifiability node may differ depending on whether emphasis is on direct identification or singling out.

title: Observing video searches and interactions discloses the child's interests and behavior
description: This flow exposes what the child searches for, requests to watch, likes, and comments on. Such data can reveal interests, emotional state, habits, and potentially special-category or otherwise sensitive inferences about the child if accessed or processed beyond what is expected.
assumptions: Assumes the service, operators, or downstream recipients can inspect or use request contents and related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected as a generic detectability/disclosure-style observation risk; exact subnode may differ by catalog version.

title: Comment and engagement history enables profiling and inference about a child
description: Accumulated searches, requests, likes, and comments can be analyzed to infer age, maturity, preferences, vulnerabilities, routines, relationships, or other traits of the child. Such derived knowledge goes beyond the explicit content of any single request.
assumptions: Assumes the service stores or analyzes historical interaction data, whether manually or algorithmically.
uncertainty_note: Chosen as an inference/profiling-related node by best judgement; exact node id may vary by threat-tree edition.

title: The child may be unaware of the extent of collection and secondary use of interaction data
description: A child user may not understand that searches, requests, likes, and comments are logged, retained, analyzed for recommendations or moderation, and possibly shared with third parties. This creates a lack of awareness about how personal data from this flow is processed.
assumptions: Assumes notices are limited, complex, or not age-appropriate for a child audience.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode for unawareness may differ by LINDDUN Pro version; applicability is strong given child users.

title: Collection and retention of child interaction data may violate child-privacy obligations
description: Processing search history, viewing requests, likes, and comments from a child can trigger strict legal and policy obligations around children's data, lawful basis/parental consent, purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, and sharing. If the service collects or reuses more data than necessary, this flow can create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the child qualifies for heightened protection under applicable law or platform policy and that this interaction data is retained or reused.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 is directly supported by retrieved context; specific legal obligation depends on jurisdiction and implementation.

title: Identified information present in stored video metadata
description: The videos collection stores video metadata, and metadata can directly contain identified information such as uploader identity, account references, filenames, titles, timestamps, location tags, or other identifiers. Even if the video file itself is the primary asset, identified metadata in the datastore can make individuals directly identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the stored metadata includes user/account identifiers or other direct identifiers linked to a person.

title: Excessive storage of personal data in video records
description: Storing both video files and associated metadata in or alongside the videos collection may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for the service purpose. Video content can reveal faces, voices, surroundings, behavior, and other sensitive contextual data, while metadata may expose additional personal details. If the flow persists unnecessary fields or retains full files where reduced data would suffice, this creates an avoidable data disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the service may store full-resolution video/media and rich metadata rather than a minimized subset strictly necessary for processing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgment based on LINDDUN Data Disclosure/minimality guidance; the exact Dd subtree citation was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Video storage may enable processing beyond user expectations
description: Users may expect videos to be stored only for immediate service delivery, but persistent storage of video content and metadata in the backend can enable additional uses such as analytics, moderation training, profiling, or long-term reuse. If those purposes are not made clear at collection time, the datastore contributes to an unlink between user expectations and actual processing.
assumptions: Assumes purposes, retention, or downstream uses of stored videos/metadata are broader than what users reasonably understand.
uncertainty_note: Applicable Unawareness threat is likely, but the exact U subtree node id is selected by best judgment because no U-specific node was included in the retrieved context.

title: Storage of video data may exceed declared purpose or retention constraints
description: Persisting video metadata and files in the datastore can conflict with consent terms, stated purpose limitation, or retention obligations if data is stored longer than necessary or reused for incompatible purposes. Because this flow is the point where records are written to storage, it is a key location for non-compliance risk if policy and legal constraints are not enforced.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy obligations around purpose limitation, retention, lawful basis, or consent conditions.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nc subtree node id is chosen by best judgment; retrieved context did not include a compliance-specific node reference.

title: Excessive retention of child search and watch history
description: The flow stores detailed child search and watch history in the childprofiles collection. This can disclose highly sensitive behavioral and preference data beyond what is strictly necessary if full histories are persistently stored rather than minimized, aggregated, or time-limited.
assumptions: Assumes the application stores granular history records tied to an identifiable child profile, and that not all retained history is strictly necessary for the service purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is based on best judgement for avoidable explicit storage/disclosure via over-collection or over-retention; exact node naming may vary by LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Linkability of child activities across sessions and content interactions
description: Persistently storing search and watch history in a child profile enables linking multiple actions, sessions, and interests to the same child over time. This may allow construction of a longitudinal behavior profile even when individual events would be less privacy-invasive in isolation.
assumptions: Assumes history entries are associated with a stable child profile identifier or other consistent key in the collection.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is chosen by best judgement; the core threat is persistent cross-event linkage in the datastore.

title: Identifiability of a child from stored viewing and search history
description: The stored history may contain distinctive combinations of queries, viewed content, timestamps, and profile attributes that make a child identifiable, either directly or by singling them out from other users.
assumptions: Assumes the collection stores profile-linked history with timestamps or rich event detail that can be associated with a specific child.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ across threat-tree versions; applicability depends on how strongly the history is tied to a child identity.

title: Detectability of sensitive child behavior from the existence of stored history
description: The mere presence, volume, or pattern of stored search/watch history can reveal that a child engaged with particular topics or content categories, even before full data contents are examined. Metadata such as record counts and timestamps can therefore expose sensitive behavior.
assumptions: Assumes datastore records or metadata are observable to some internal components, operators, or through side channels beyond the strict need-to-know scope.
uncertainty_note: Detectability here is based on metadata and record existence rather than content disclosure; exact tree-node id is approximate.

title: Unawareness of storage of child search and watch history
description: Children or their guardians may be unaware that detailed search and watch history is being stored in the childprofiles collection, for what purposes, and for how long. This undermines transparency and informed expectations about profiling and personalization.
assumptions: Assumes transparency notices, age-appropriate explanations, or parental controls may be incomplete or insufficiently prominent.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on the surrounding notice and UX context, which is not shown in the DFD; included because the flow clearly performs storage of potentially unexpected child activity data.

title: Non-compliant storage of child behavioral history
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate data-minimization, purpose-limitation, retention, or child-specific consent/guardian-authorization requirements if the history is not strictly necessary, is retained too long, or is processed without an appropriate legal basis.
assumptions: Assumes the data concerns children and may therefore be subject to heightened regulatory requirements and stricter lawful-processing conditions.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction, ages, purposes, and implemented consent/retention controls; exact node id is approximate.

title: Insufficient provability of consent and history-management actions
description: If child search and watch history is stored without reliable records of parental consent, notice delivery, or later deletion/objection actions, the system may be unable to prove what privacy-relevant actions were authorized or performed. This creates repudiation risk around the legitimacy of storing the history.
assumptions: Assumes the service requires consent or other auditable authorization for storing child behavioral history and that such evidence may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: This is included cautiously because the DFD flow alone does not show consent or audit mechanisms; exact applicability depends on product and legal context.

title: Uploaded video and metadata may identify the parent or child beyond what is necessary
description: The upload flow can carry directly identifying content in the video itself (faces, voices, home interior, school uniforms) and metadata associated with approval/rejection. If the service accepts or retains excessive identifying data for moderation, the parent user and possibly the child become readily identifiable to the service or downstream reviewers.
assumptions: Assumes uploaded videos contain personal data and that P2 stores or exposes associated metadata during the approval workflow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context confirms Identifiability applies to ExternalEntity->Process flows but does not provide the exact subtree citation.

title: Video upload content may disclose sensitive personal information during moderation
description: A submitted video can reveal special-category or otherwise sensitive information about the child or household, such as health conditions, religious indicators, precise location cues, routines, or socioeconomic context. The approval/rejection process may expose this content to moderators or internal roles that do not strictly need full access.
assumptions: Assumes human or automated review occurs inside P2 and that full video content is accessible for approval decisions.
uncertainty_note: Exact D subtree node is selected by best judgement because the supplied context does not include disclosure subtrees.

title: Insufficient proof of upload submission or approval/rejection decision
description: If the service does not keep reliable, privacy-appropriate evidence of who submitted a video, when it was submitted, and what approval/rejection decision was communicated, either party may later deny the action or dispute the outcome. This can undermine complaint handling and data-subject rights resolution.
assumptions: Assumes the platform needs an auditable record of submissions and moderation outcomes.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is applicable to this interaction per mapping; exact subtree citation is approximate.

title: Parent may be unaware of how uploaded videos are reviewed, retained, or reused
description: During upload and approval/rejection, the service may fail to provide clear information about moderation criteria, who can view the video, retention periods, reuse for training or quality assurance, or consequences of rejection. This leaves the parent insufficiently informed about the processing of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes transparency notices are incomplete or not presented in context at upload time.
uncertainty_note: Exact Unawareness subtree node is selected by best judgement.

title: Approval workflow may process children's video data without compliant data-management controls
description: Because the flow involves user-uploaded video likely containing children's personal data, the service may become non-compliant if it lacks an appropriate lawful basis, age-appropriate notices, purpose limitation, retention limits, reviewer access controls, or procedures for handling rejected content. Improper management of these videos and associated decisions creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to privacy/data-protection obligations and the upload may include children's personal data.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 is directly supported by the retrieved context; specific legal obligations depend on jurisdiction and product details.

title: Video stream metadata may identify or profile the child
description: The outbound video stream can expose identifying or profiling information about the child through account-specific URLs, session identifiers, device-adaptive manifests, subtitles/preferences, or other metadata embedded in or accompanying the stream. Even if the content is approved, the delivered flow may reveal who the child is or what profile is active.
assumptions: Assumes the streaming response or associated delivery metadata contains persistent or user-specific identifiers, or otherwise reveals child profile information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement for identifiability at the data-flow level; exact subtree id may vary by LINDDUN Pro edition.

title: Viewing behavior can be disclosed to parties observing the stream delivery
description: Sending the approved video to the child can disclose that this specific child account is watching a particular video at a particular time. Network observers, CDN/logging infrastructure, or downstream recipients with access to delivery records may infer viewing habits and interests from the stream flow.
assumptions: Assumes stream requests, delivery logs, or observable traffic patterns are available to parties beyond the child and strictly necessary service components.
uncertainty_note: Threat is grounded in disclosure of personal viewing activity via the Process→ExternalEntity flow; exact node id is best-effort.

title: Child may be unaware of personal data embedded in streaming and telemetry
description: The child receiving the stream may be unaware that the delivery can include embedded identifiers, personalization markers, tracking beacons, or telemetry related to playback. This reduces transparency about what personal data is being conveyed or generated as part of the streaming interaction.
assumptions: Assumes the service includes analytics, personalization, or other data elements beyond the raw video bytes.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether telemetry or personalized metadata accompanies the stream; if the flow is strictly anonymous content delivery, this may not apply.

title: Streaming more personal data than necessary to the child may violate data-minimization obligations
description: If the service delivers the video together with unnecessary personal data, persistent identifiers, detailed recommendation context, or excessive tracking information, the flow may fail data-minimization and purpose-limitation requirements for children's data processing.
assumptions: Assumes children's privacy obligations apply and that the stream may carry ancillary personal data not strictly required to render the approved video.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 is supported by the provided context; compliance impact depends on jurisdiction and actual stream contents.

title: Excessive child-profile data disclosure to recommendation engine
description: The planned flow sends child browsing data from the childprofiles collection to the AI Recommendation Engine. If the engine receives full browsing histories or profile attributes beyond what is strictly necessary for generating recommendations, personal data about children is unnecessarily disclosed to another processing component, violating data minimisation.
assumptions: Assumes the AI engine does not need the full raw child browsing dataset and that a reduced or aggregated feature set could serve the purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimisation structure; exact subnode citation may vary by threat-tree edition.

title: Inference of sensitive child traits from browsing data
description: By ingesting child browsing histories, the AI Recommendation Engine may infer additional sensitive characteristics about a child, such as interests, vulnerabilities, age-related traits, habits, or special-category proxies, beyond the data explicitly stored in the source collection. This creates an identifiability/inference privacy risk at the receiving process.
assumptions: Assumes the recommendation model performs profiling or feature extraction over granular browsing events.
uncertainty_note: Using 'I' for inference/identifiability risk is a best-fit judgement; exact node id may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Linkability of child activity across sessions or contexts in the AI engine
description: Combining browsing data from the childprofiles collection inside the AI Recommendation Engine may allow the engine to link multiple browsing events, sessions, devices, or profile records to the same child, enabling richer tracking than originally apparent from isolated records.
assumptions: Assumes records include stable identifiers or sufficiently unique behavioural patterns to support correlation.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode id is approximate; threat applicability is strong even if numbering differs.

title: Opaque AI processing of child browsing data
description: If child browsing data is fed into the recommendation engine without clear explanation to parents or children, the subsequent profiling and recommendation logic may be insufficiently transparent. Data subjects may not understand what data is used, how recommendations are produced, or what consequences follow from this processing.
assumptions: Assumes the planned AI use is not fully explained in notices or UI at the time of collection or use.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort based on unawareness/lack-of-transparency concepts in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Potential incompatibility with children's consent and purpose-limitation requirements
description: Using child browsing data from the childprofiles collection for AI recommendations may exceed the originally communicated purpose or rely on an invalid legal basis for children's data processing. This creates a non-compliance risk, especially where parental consent, fairness, age-appropriate design, or purpose limitation obligations apply.
assumptions: Assumes the AI recommendation purpose is planned/new and may not yet be covered by existing notices, consent records, or governance controls.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode numbering is approximate; threat is grounded in LINDDUN non-compliance/privacy-requirements concerns.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The planned flow sends browsing data from the recommendation engine to external advertisers. Browsing data is personal data and sharing it with third parties for advertising may exceed what is strictly necessary for providing recommendations, creating an explicit and avoidable disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the browsing data can relate to an identifiable or singlable user, directly or indirectly, and that advertisers are third parties distinct from the primary service provider.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality guidance; exact sub-node labeling may vary across versions.

title: Cross-context linkability via advertiser data sharing
description: Sending browsing data to advertisers can enable them to correlate this user's activity on the system with profiles, identifiers, or events observed elsewhere, making otherwise separate interactions linkable across services and contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the shared payload includes persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, cookies, device data, or sufficiently distinctive behavioral attributes that advertisers can match with existing profiles.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may differ; threat applicability is strong even if the specific tree-node id is approximate.

title: Identifiability of users from shared browsing data
description: Browsing data shared with advertisers may directly identify users or allow re-identification when combined with other data already held by the advertiser. Even pseudonymous event streams can become identifying when enriched with external datasets.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers possess auxiliary data and the browsing data contains direct identifiers, stable pseudonyms, or rich behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Sub-node id is selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the relevant identifiability tree.

title: Detectability of user activity by third-party advertisers
description: The very transmission of browsing events to advertisers makes user activity observable to those third parties. Advertisers may detect that a user visited certain pages, interacted with particular content, or belongs to sensitive audience segments, even if full identification is not immediate.
assumptions: Assumes the flow contains event-level or segment-level browsing information rather than only fully aggregated statistics.
uncertainty_note: Specific detectability sub-node may be approximate; threat relevance to this planned event-sharing flow is high.

title: Potential non-compliance due to third-party advertising data sharing
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate privacy principles or legal obligations if there is no valid legal basis, informed consent, purpose limitation, transparency, or data-minimization justification. Planned disclosures to ad-tech recipients are particularly sensitive from a compliance perspective.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy/data-protection obligations and that browsing data is personal data or can become personal data in context.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance sub-node id may differ by LINDDUN Pro version; the compliance risk itself is well grounded.

title: Excessive retention of government ID images in file storage
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data. Storing full-resolution ID images in backend/uploads/ can create avoidable data disclosure risk if the files are retained longer than strictly necessary for identity verification or kept beyond the purpose for which they were collected.
assumptions: Assumes the uploaded ID images are persisted in DS4 rather than immediately transformed into a less sensitive verification result and deleted.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selection is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data disclosure/minimality concepts; the retrieved context did not include the exact subtree text.

title: Over-collection of raw identity-document images
description: This flow stores raw government ID images in a filesystem datastore. If the service only needs specific attributes or a verification outcome, storing complete document images discloses more personal data than necessary, including photo, document number, nationality, address, or machine-readable zones.
assumptions: Assumes business purpose could potentially be satisfied by extracting required fields or storing a tokenized verification result instead of the entire image.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate; grounded in the LINDDUN minimality principle for avoidable explicit disclosure.

title: Unexpected secondary use of stored ID images
description: Users may reasonably expect ID images to be used only for immediate identity verification. Persisting the images in a general backend uploads area may enable later reuse for debugging, model training, fraud analytics, manual review, or other secondary purposes that are not apparent from the upload action.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit, granular user expectation-setting limits downstream uses of the stored images.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subtree id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include unlinkability/awareness tree details.

title: Storage of ID images may exceed user consent or legal basis scope
description: If users consented to authentication or age/identity checking, persisting the full government ID image in backend/uploads/ may exceed the scope of that consent or another legal basis unless storage duration, purpose, and downstream access are clearly justified and communicated.
assumptions: Assumes this flow relies on consent or another purpose-limited legal basis and that long-term file storage is not inherently obvious to the user.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node id is approximate; threat applicability depends on the system's stated legal basis, notice, and retention policy.

title: JWT in localStorage can disclose user identity and session claims to scripts with same-origin access
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage makes its contents accessible to any JavaScript executing in the same origin, including third-party scripts or injected script. If the token contains user identifiers, roles, email, subject claims, or other personal data, the destination datastore causes identifiability disclosure by exposing those claims beyond the strictly necessary authentication context.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is readable client-side and contains identifying or user-related claims rather than being an opaque reference token.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgment from general LINDDUN Pro disclosure taxonomy; exact node id may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Persistent JWT storage enables cross-session linkability of user activity within the origin
description: A JWT persisted in localStorage can serve as a stable identifier across page loads and browser sessions. Scripts on the same origin can reuse the token or its stable subject/session claims to correlate a user's actions over time, increasing linkability beyond what is necessary for a single authentication event.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT persists beyond the current page lifecycle and includes a stable identifier or is itself reused as a stable token.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ across versions; applicability is strong because persistent client-side tokens are classic linkability enablers.

title: JWT contents and storage metadata reveal sensitive personal information
description: When a JWT is stored in localStorage, not only the token value but also associated metadata such as presence, key names, timing of creation, and embedded claims may reveal private information. Depending on token payload, this can disclose authentication status, account type, tenant membership, or other personal attributes to code with same-origin access.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted end-to-end for the browser and may contain readable claims or inferable account metadata.
uncertainty_note: This threat overlaps with disclosure/identifiability; classified as detectability of private attributes because mere observation of storage state may reveal user state.

title: Client-side persistent token storage may violate data minimization or secure-storage obligations
description: Persisting an authentication JWT in localStorage may be non-compliant with privacy or security requirements if long-lived authentication data is stored client-side without adequate safeguards, retention limits, or justification. This can conflict with obligations to minimize personal data exposure, limit retention, and use appropriate protection for authentication artifacts tied to individuals.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policy, regulatory, or organizational requirements constrain storage location, retention, or protection of authentication tokens linked to users.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact is context-dependent and depends on the governing policy/regulatory framework.

title: Excessive child history disclosed to parent
description: When Child Profile Management retrieves and sends child history for parent review, the flow may include more history than is necessary for the review purpose (for example, full historical records, sensitive notes, or data about unrelated contexts). This would expose personal information beyond what the parent should receive in this interaction.
assumptions: Assumes the child history can contain sensitive or broad historical data and that role- or purpose-based filtering may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgment for over-disclosure of content on a flow; exact node numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent can infer sensitive aspects of the child from retrieved history
description: The returned history may allow the parent to infer additional sensitive attributes or situations about the child beyond the explicitly presented facts, such as health, behavioral patterns, location routines, relationships, or special circumstances. Even if each item is acceptable on its own, the combined history can reveal more than intended.
assumptions: Assumes the history spans multiple events or categories so that patterns or sensitive conclusions can be drawn.
uncertainty_note: Applicable because this flow explicitly delivers historical data for review; exact threat-tree node citation is approximate.

title: Historical records can be linked into a detailed child profile
description: Delivering child history to the parent enables linking of multiple events, timestamps, and categories into a richer profile of the child. This aggregation can reveal behavior patterns, habits, and long-term characteristics that would not be evident from isolated records.
assumptions: Assumes multiple historical entries share identifiers, timestamps, or other quasi-identifiers that support correlation.
uncertainty_note: The linking risk is strongly supported by LINDDUN methodology, but the exact node id is an approximate best-fit.

title: Third-party or sibling data may be disclosed within the child's history
description: The child history returned for parent review may contain information not only about the child but also about other data subjects, such as siblings, classmates, caregivers, reporters, or staff mentioned in notes or event context. Sending such mixed records to the parent could disclose others' personal data without need or authorization.
assumptions: Assumes free-text notes, event context, or shared activity records can include data about additional people.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree node numbering is approximate; threat applicability depends on whether history records can embed third-party data.

title: Parent may be unaware of the extent and sensitivity of child history disclosed
description: If the system presents the child history without clear explanation of what categories are included, over what time period, and why, the parent may not understand the scope and privacy implications of the data being shown. Lack of transparency can undermine informed expectations about the child's data use and review.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or accompanying notice does not clearly explain the composition and rationale of the retrieved history.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible unawareness threat on the receiving side of the flow, but the exact node id is an approximate best-fit.

title: Child history may be used for a review purpose beyond the child's or guardian's reasonable expectations
description: Retrieving and presenting detailed child history to a parent may be incompatible with the original purpose for which some history items were collected, especially if data gathered for operational, educational, safeguarding, or health-related purposes are repurposed for generalized parental review without appropriate legal basis, minimization, or policy constraints.
assumptions: Assumes history items may originate from multiple collection purposes and not all are necessarily compatible with parent-facing review.
uncertainty_note: Exact node numbering is approximate; applicability depends on system purpose limitation and governance design.

title: Insufficient evidence of what child history was disclosed to the parent
description: If the system does not create reliable records of which child history items were retrieved and shown to the parent, it may later be impossible to demonstrate or contest whether particular personal data was disclosed. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant disclosures.
assumptions: Assumes disclosure logging for parent review is absent, incomplete, or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is included by the mapping table for this interaction, but whether this becomes a meaningful privacy issue depends on logging/accountability requirements.
